summary: MODEL_CHANGE_REQUIRED: the update moves DIFF logging before the NEWLEADER ACK and starts processors in a non-serving INITIAL state. The model, trace harness and update lens were updated; 13 fresh traces validate. Model checking found three defects, all reproduced on the updated code: the ACK still precedes durability, an UPTODATE-time failure leaves a stale in-memory database that can lead without a committed transaction, and a txn ACK can shadow the NEWLEADER ACK.
validation_limits: Model checking is finite-bound and time-budgeted (3 servers, 1 txn, 2-3 epochs, <=2 crashes); no run is a proof. The standard round exhausted its depth-23 space only with the analysed MC-2 class filtered.
Update property P2 was not reached by 3-server full/focused BFS within budget (depth 26 of about 28); it is covered by a 2-server hunt and by full-MCNext simulation.
Trace.tla is the inherited observation-projection validator; V1 events are checked by explicit post-state predicates, not by replaying base actions.
Learner process crashes were emulated by a stalled SyncRequestProcessor plus restart (MC-1); MC-3 was reproduced only with an injected learner-thread pause.
Open-spec checking is provisional: it violated P1 like the concrete focused spec; discharge of omitted context found no violation within budget.

findings.title: NEWLEADER ACK is written before the synced transactions are durable
findings.cause: Learner.syncWithLeader persists the new epoch, enqueues the buffered sync proposals with logRequest, and writes the NEWLEADER ACK before SyncRequestProcessor appends and forces them.
findings.trigger: A learner DIFF-syncs a transaction held only by the new leader, ACKs NEWLEADER, and stops before its log flush; the leader is then lost.
findings.consequence: The leader serves the transaction on a quorum that never persisted it; the learner's newer epoch wins the next election and the committed transaction disappears.

premises: The NEWLEADER ACK is written before any synchronous flush
A crashed learner can lose appended-but-unflushed txn log bytes

findings.title: Failure between NEWLEADER ACK and UPTODATE leaves the server INITIAL; shutdown is skipped and the stale in-memory DB is used to vote and lead
findings.cause: startupWithoutServing leaves State.INITIAL; canShutdown() is false for it, so shutdown skips the database fast-forward and the processor shutdown.
findings.trigger: Learners ACK NEWLEADER, fail before UPTODATE, and re-elect in-process after the old leader stops.
findings.consequence: A new leader elected from the stale in-memory history omits a transaction the old leader committed and served; leaked processors also write it into the log behind the served history.

premises: getLastLoggedZxid and Leader.lead use the initialized in-memory database

findings.title: A learner txn ACK can precede its NEWLEADER ACK
findings.cause: The NEWLEADER branch starts SyncRequestProcessor and SendAckRequestProcessor before the learner writes the NEWLEADER ACK.
findings.trigger: The learner thread is delayed after logRequest while the sync thread flushes and acknowledges a DIFF txn.
findings.consequence: LearnerHandler takes the txn ACK as the NEWLEADER ACK and rejects it, so the learner is never counted and the leader cannot establish its epoch.

premises: Processors are started before the NEWLEADER ACK write
LearnerHandler treats the first ACK after NEWLEADER as the NEWLEADER ACK
